oneliner.t: Libertarian from Fairbanks, a retired Air Force master sergeant, writer and former small-business instructor, making his fourth run for Alaska's House seat; he finished eighth in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary (1.2%) and moved onto the November ballot after four higher finishers withdrew.

born.note: Both are his own pamphlet/questionnaire answers; exact date not published.

upbringing.t: Born in Savannah, Georgia. He served about 22 years in the U.S. Air Force, retiring as a master sergeant; his last assignment brought him to Anchorage, where he stayed (1991–2006) before moving to Fairbanks in 2006. After the military he worked as a DeVry University recruiter, an enrollment specialist at UAA, director of the Small Business Development Center in Fairbanks, and an instructor at UAF. He is married and has three sons, writes children's books, and in his pamphlet statement calls Jesus Christ the greatest teacher of all time.

profile.office_note: Gov. Dunleavy appointed him to the Alaska Public Offices Commission in 2019, but the Legislature did not confirm him (April 2019); whether he sat on the commission before the vote is not documented, so 0 years is recorded.

career.yrs: ≈22½ years, ending around his 1991 arrival in Anchorage (exact dates not documented)
career.role: Noncommissioned officer, retired as Master Sergeant
College recruiter / enrollment advisor; enrollment services specialist
career.org: DeVry University; University of Alaska Anchorage

career.role: Writer; school tutor at Fort Wainwright

platform.t: Personal liberty is his top issue; small government works best; free markets but no crony capitalism; fewer regulations on small businesses.
Supports term limits to remove career politicians.
Outside audits of how tax dollars are spent; opposes IRS intimidation.
At least 50% of annual PFD payouts should go to Alaskans rather than government.
Supports the military but opposes nation-building and 'perpetual wars'.
A more open, vetted green-card process for law-abiding immigrants.
Supports Trump's tariffs as leveling trade.
A personal decision; government should step back.
Vetted, trained armed security at schools and public places plus aggressive action on illegal guns.
Likes the idea of able-bodied people working at least part time.
Supports security aid to allies, including Ukraine, without U.S. ground troops.
Parents should have a say in schools; supports well-trained officers who live in the communities they serve; supports mental-health clinics.

promises.t: Make personal liberties the core of his work in Congress.
Won't commit to either party's caucus; would seek like-minded lawmakers.

claims.claim: Served about 22½ years in the U.S. Air Force, retiring as a Master Sergeant.

record.t: KNOM (2016) reported 22 years and the rank of Master Sergeant; the Beacon (2026) calls him a former Air Force NCO. Both rely on his account; no service record was reviewed.

claims.claim: Government service: Election Commissioner, Alaska Public Offices Commission.

said.where: 2026 Official Election Pamphlet (bio); Beacon survey lists 'former AK Elections Commissioner'

record.t: Gov. Dunleavy appointed James McDermott of Fairbanks to APOC in 2019, but the Legislature did not confirm him in April 2019 amid a dispute over whether the seat had to go to a Democrat. Any service before that vote is not documented, and APOC regulates campaign finance and disclosure, not elections.

claims.claim: Term and adjunct business instructor, UAF School of Management.

record.t: KNOM (2016) reported he had taught at UAF since 2008.

claims.claim: College recruiter and enrollment advisor, DeVry University.

record.t: KNOM (2016) reported the same, plus UAA enrollment work.

claims.claim: Lived in Anchorage January 1991–March 2006 and Fairbanks since March 2006.

record.t: The Beacon reports he moved to Fairbanks in 2006 after 15 years in Anchorage.

claims.claim: M.S., University of La Verne; B.S., Wayland Baptist University.

entries.t: Said he would not have cut residents' dividends in half to close the budget gap.
At least 50% of annual PFD payouts should go to the people.
Regulate marijuana like alcohol; shift spending from incarceration to substance-abuse education.
Supported developing alternatives to oil, including natural gas, wind and solar.

statements.t: Supports security aid to allies when asked about aid to Israel.

fec.src_note: FEC lists election years 2012, 2014, 2016 and 2026 but shows no 2025–26 financial data and no principal committee on the candidate page.

support: Cornerstone Founders PAC — $463,000 on ads promoting Republican Clay Strickland and Libertarian McDermott (split not reported)

fec.outside_note: ADN (Aug. 2026) reported Cornerstone Founders PAC, which had not disclosed its backers, spent $463,000 on ads promoting Strickland and 'Libertarian Clay McDermott' (an apparent name error for Jim McDermott, the only McDermott in the race). How much promoted McDermott is not reported, and the PAC's FEC page was not opened.

history.note: FEC: 'We don't have MCDERMOTT, JIM C for 2011–2012.'
coverage 2013-01-01 to 2014-11-19; statement of candidacy filed 2014-09-26

money_flags_note: Not a clean finding. His own committee shows only $7,877 raised (2014) and nothing for 2012 or 2026; 2016 not retrieved. Cornerstone Founders PAC's backers are undisclosed in reporting, so whether corporate money paid for ads promoting him can't be determined. No pro-Israel or other foreign-policy PAC money found.

superpac_donors.note: Spending shared with Strickland; donors undisclosed per ADN.

note.t: No House candidate financial disclosure for him was searched or found.

democracy.t: Asked who won the 2020 election, he cited ballot harvesting, secret counting and unguarded ballot collection as reasons for doubt and called for restoring election integrity; he did not name a winner in the summary reviewed.
Supports federal involvement in state voter data, citing invalid voter rolls; supports ranked-choice voting.

note.t: In Alaska since January 1991 (Anchorage to 2006, Fairbanks since).

checks.legal: No court, CourtListener or Alaska CourtView search was run; no legal matters surfaced in the news coverage reviewed.
checks.foreign: No disclosure or FARA search run; no foreign ties surfaced in sources reviewed.
checks.claims: Campaign site could not be opened. Mechanical sample = every checkable claim in his paid 2026 Official Election Pamphlet bio. 7 rated: 5 true, 1 partly, 1 unverifiable. No ads found.
checks.democracy: Beacon 2026 questionnaire. Never held elected office.

research_notes: Primary Aug. 18, 2026: 1,951 votes (1.2%), eighth of 15; advanced after Schultz, J. Williams, Strickland and Reynoso withdrew. He learned he had made the ballot from the Alaska Beacon. The Beacon corrected its story: this is his fourth general-election appearance for the seat (2012, 2014, 2016, 2026), not his second. The KTOO 2019 APOC story names 'James McDermott, a Fairbanks resident' and Libertarian; matched to him by name, city and party. Photo not retrieved.
